# About me

::: {#about-content}
Hi! I’m Milena, a quantitative researcher interested in how social environments shape individual outcomes and inequality. I work with population-scale administrative data and survey data, applying methods from psychometrics and measurement to multilevel modelling and social network analysis.

I started in psychology at **Maastricht University** because I wanted to understand behaviour in context, and found myself most at home on the quantitative side. Especially the challenge of measuring things that cannot be observed directly, like well-being or trust. A master’s in Statistics and Data Science at **Leiden University** taught me statistical modelling, measurement, and working with complex data. For my master’s thesis at **Statistics Netherlands (CBS)**, I worked with linked administrative registers covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents, investigating how people’s embeddedness across social domains such as work, neighbourhood, and household relates to their willingness to trust others.

I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen. There, I spent two years working as an au pair caring for three young children, while studying Dutch at KU Leuven. Being part of their daily lives in a context so different from my own made me curious about how much our surroundings shape who we become. I am based in Leiden and open to research-oriented roles in the Netherlands where I can apply quantitative methods to relevant social questions.

In my free time, you will find me taking care of my lovely tropical plants, working in the garden, and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, reading about different perspectives, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
:::
